public_rationale: CNBC reported that Alphabet on October 28 and Amazon on October 29, 2026 missed LSEG revenue and EPS expectations for July–September; Alphabet's EPS comparison used adjusted earnings [e1, e2]. Amazon reported AWS sales growth of 39% year over year, compared with 6% for North America and 5% for International, supporting AWS as its growth standout [e3]. The supplied Alphabet evidence does not establish the corresponding business-line growth comparison [e1]. The reports also do not establish billions in recognized quarterly compute revenue attributable to both named labs, leaving the full claim unresolved [e1, e2, e3].
limitations: The consensus comparisons rely on CNBC's reporting of LSEG estimates [e1, e2].
Amazon's segment comparison does not establish Google Cloud's relative growth [e3].
The evidence does not provide a period-matched breakdown of recognized compute revenue from Anthropic and OpenAI at each provider [e1, e2, e3].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: In the same week, Amazon and Google both had double-misses on earnings, and only their cloud businesses, which are inflated by billions of dollars of Anthropic and OpenAI compute spend, showed any exciting growth.

statement.excerpt: The same week, Amazon and Google both had double-misses on earnings, with only their cloud businesses — which are inflated by billions of dollars of compute spend from both Anthropic and OpenAI — showing any exciting growth.

from_speaker: Amazon and Google both had double-misses on earnings
billions of dollars of compute spend from both Anthropic and OpenAI
our_interpretation: Double-miss means quarterly revenue and earnings per share below contemporaneous analyst consensus.
The context identifies the earnings announcements in October 26 through November 1, 2026; the operating results concern July through September 2026.
The ordinary reading of exciting growth is that cloud was the clear growth standout. No numerical threshold is imposed.
Inflated means increased by recognized compute sales to the named labs; it does not by itself allege improper accounting.
The claim combines two companies and several financial measures. Individual evidence scopes are retained rather than treating one company's results as evidence for the other.
Estimate describes the consensus-comparison basis. Company-reported growth and realized customer spending must be assessed separately.
criteria.support_condition: Both companies missed revenue and comparable EPS consensus in the specified announcement week; cloud was the clear growth standout; and period-matched records establish billions in recognized compute sales attributable to the named labs.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records show that either company did not have a double-miss, that non-cloud businesses had similarly standout growth, or that the claimed lab spending attribution is materially incorrect.

evidence.explanation: Amazon's release establishes AWS as a growth standout relative to its retail segments. It does not attribute that growth to particular lab customers.
